lexical.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.

pairs_touching.homonym_positive_evidence: S0091: the corpus explicitly splits the single naive concept 'Communication' into two distinct, independently-verified capabilities C-10 and C-19, each with its own responsibility, existence test, and state model (S0101, S0102).
pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: They remain structurally linked in one control loop (S0102/S0234: BC-1 policy/knowledge -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES), hence PARTIALLY-COMPATIBLE rather than INCOMPATIBLE -- sequential pipeline neighbors, not fully unrelated, but confirmed-distinct capabilities rather than the same one under two names.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: S0091 (shared verbatim in both samples) is a direct SOURCE-CLAIMED-SEPARATION row: "'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition...". S0101 (also shared) independently verifies 'the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities.' S0102 further shows different responsibility and no simple continuity: C-19 fails six of ten bounded-context criteria while C-10 has its own seven-state receipt/delivery lifecycle -- distinct formal models for what a naive reading once called one 'Communication' capability.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a later ruling recombines C-10 and C-19 into one capability after all (reversing the split), or shows C-19 is simply a downstream phase of C-10's own lifecycle rather than a genuinely separate capability, this would move toward CONTINUATION or SPECIALIZATION instead.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Sibling capabilities in one control loop (C-5/C-10/C-14/C-19), analogous to the S0237/S0239 candidate-register co-listing pattern noted in the task instructions.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Heavy CO-OCCURRENCE (4x) and five shared source_ids (S0091, S0101, S0102, S0168, S0234), but every shared row treats C-14 and C-19 as two DIFFERENT capabilities co-listed in the same 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) and the same 4-capability unowned control loop: 'BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome' (S0102/S0234). C-19 additionally fails 6 of 10 bounded-context-test criteria and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, structurally distinct from C-14's enforcement-gate role. No row claims C-14 and C-19 are the same, or that one is a refinement/extension of the other -- this is the same-registry co-listing pattern (large capability inventory, coincidental co-tagging), not a lineage relation.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row proposing C-14 and C-19 be merged into a single capability (rather than four capabilities in one control loop) would change this to SAME or REDEFINITION.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: A and B are both entries drawn from the same 20-capability census (S0091/S0234, C-1..C-20) of capabilities lacking a bounded-context owner. S0234 places them in one control loop (BC-1 DEFINES -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS), i.e. a functional dependency between two distinct, co-listed capabilities in the same registry -- matching the task's flagged 'shared candidate-register census row' pattern that is insufficient alone for identity/evolution.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row explicitly stating C-19 is a refinement/specialization/extension of C-5 (rather than a distinct capability feeding it in a control loop) would change this.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: why_grouped (POSSIBLY-RELATION) states governance-communication-candidate (b) is 'an untracked C4 actor/component naming a communication concern inside Governance; disposed of as a concurring sketch, not evidence, and explicitly not converted into governed architecture by the six-role adoption act.' a (capability-c19-communication-composition) is instead a ratified item in the 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20), independently verified (S0101) and structurally placed in a four-capability control loop (S0102). b was explicitly rejected/never formalized, so no claim connects it to a's established capability.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row stating the disposed-of governance-communication sketch was the origin of, or was folded into, C-19 would establish DERIVED-FROM or REPLACEMENT.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
rationale_evidence.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
rationale_evidence.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
rationale_evidence.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

rationale_evidence.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
rationale_evidence.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

rationale_evidence.anchor: DDD does not define a bounded context by noun category or organizational role ... Communication becomes a bounded context when it has its own domain language ... a reason to evolve separately.
rationale_evidence.statement: Challenges creating a Communication bounded context merely because a Communication Engineer role exists; a Communication context is defensible only if messages/audiences/consent/delivery/retention carry independent domain invariants and lifecycle, not merely presentation/rendering.

Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). Flagged as a proposal finding, not adopted architecture; C-10/C-14 existence remain UNDECIDED.

## Rationale
Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles [S0091]. 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor [S0091]. Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them [S0102]. C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context [S0102]. Challenges creating a Communication bounded context merely because a Communication Engineer role exists; a Communication context is defensible only if messages/audiences/consent/delivery/retention carry independent domain invariants and lifecycle, not merely presentation/rendering [S0168]. Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). Flagged as a proposal finding, not adopted architecture; C-10/C-14 existence remain UNDECIDED [S0234].
